dossier.public_summary: The light-curve shows two very different dip depths that alternate between odd and even events and the dip depth also changes strongly from one TESS sector to another. Together with a long, grazing eclipse shape, this matches a stellar binary eclipsing the target star at about twice the 11.9-day period, not a planet.

reasons.why: Odd and even depths differ strongly (33.76 vs 359.3 ppm, ratio 11, difference 0.906) with diff_sigma 8.577 and red_noise 1.351, consistent with an eclipsing binary at twice the 11.9 d period (23.8 d) rather than a planet at 11.9 d.

Depth changes dramatically between sectors (depth_change_pct 275.2%, -40 ppm in sector 44 to 481 ppm in sector 45) highly non-steady; inconsistent with a planet at a single period and consistent with sector-dependent folding of two different depths.

High impact parameter (b 0.8089, v_sigma 1.498) and star_density_penalty 50.85 indicate a grazing geometry not expected for a 1.118 Rearth planet; favours stellar eclipse on target rather than small planet.
Observed duration 4.996 h vs central 3.199 h ratio 1.562 stretches beyond a central transit, and duration.ratio 1.562 with this grazing shape supports binary interpretation.

Centroid is inconclusive with no clear difference image, and neighbours has plausible_within_1px 0 with closest that could at 48.6 arcsec needing 0.0771 eclipse, leaving a grazing eclipsing binary on the target as the best explanation, not a neighbour blend.
